## Highlights since 0.19.0

- **Your Agent conversations come along to the native Lattice.** The native Lattice now shows the Agent conversations you had in the classic version, with their messages and attachments, without anything to do. Each time its Agent starts, it adds the classic version's conversations it doesn't have yet, including ones started there after a switch back, and a short notice says how many. It only reads the classic version's data, never changes it, and leaves the conversations you started in the native Lattice as they are. Continuing an imported conversation picks up from its earlier messages, but not from the tool calls, checkpoints or session the classic version had.
- **Overleaf merges your co-authors' edits sentence by sentence.** When you and a co-author both changed a file between syncs, Lattice now merges the two against the last synced version, sentence by sentence in prose, so edits to different sentences of the same paragraph both survive. Only a spot you both rewrote is marked, right in the file, with This Mac and Overleaf's text side by side and **Keep mine**, **Keep theirs** or **Keep both** on it; no "(local conflict …)" copy is written beside it any more. When a figure or other binary file changed on both sides, the newer copy stays, and a notice offers **Use mine** or **Use Overleaf's** to swap. The PDF of every main document in the project now stays on this Mac, not only the first one's.
- **The Agent in a window of its own.** In the native Lattice, **Open in separate window** in the Agent panel's header moves the Agent into its own window, with its conversation, your draft and a running reply intact. **Return to workspace**, or closing the window, puts it back. The window keeps its place and size for each project, and reopens with the project.
- **Archived conversations, back where you can find them.** Settings › Agent › Archived threads lists the Agent conversations you closed with ×, and the ones archived after a while unused, in both versions of Lattice. Restore one to bring it back into the Agent's history, or delete it for good.

## Notable fixes

- Overleaf sync no longer stops at a file whose name Overleaf refuses, such as one with a backslash: that file stays on this Mac, everything else keeps syncing, and a warning names it and says why. Lattice also never writes a bibliography to such a path.
- In the native Lattice, pasting or typing in the Agent's message box while a .tex file is open goes to the message box, not into the document.
- In the native Lattice, scrolling over the gap between two panels no longer puts up a tall white "Release to focus" bar over the editor.
- A tab for a file Lattice doesn't know, such as a .docx or a .zip, shows a plain file icon instead of none, or a picture.
- In live preview, a figure caption you edit no longer flashes at the body text's size before it settles.
- The Agent's conversation history menu opens properly when the panel is wide.
- Updates now come from Lattice's new home on GitHub, lattice-writer/lattice, with the old address as a fallback.
- On Linux, the browser version can run behind a reverse proxy: `--browser-public-origin` names the exact address it is served at.
